asset_explanations.caption: Figure 2: The overall architecture of our model. “mr” means metaphor recognition, “sa” means sentiment analysis, “id” means intention detection, “od” means offensiveness detection.
asset_explanations.summary: Figure 2 illustrates the overall architecture of a multimodal model designed for meme understanding. The system processes text inputs (source/target domains and literal text) and image inputs (full images and detected objects) through separate encoders. These features are fused and processed through a 'global-local interaction' module involving cross-modal attention blocks ($CAP_{G-T}$ and $CAP_{G-I}$) across multiple layers. Finally, the model aggregates these features to predict four downstream tasks: metaphor recognition (mr), sentiment analysis (sa), intention detection (id), and offensiveness detection (od).

asset_explanations.caption: Table 1: Experimental results on the MET-MEME dataset of four tasks.
asset_explanations.summary: This table reports experimental results on the MET-MEME dataset for four tasks: Sentiment Analysis, Intention Detection, Offensiveness Detection, and Metaphor Recognition, in both English and Chinese. It compares ten baseline methods (VGG16, DenseNet-161, ResNet-50, Multi-BERT_EfficientNet, Multi-BERT_ViT, Multi-BERT_PiT, MET_add, MET_cat, M3F_add, M3F_cat) against a proposed method (Ours). Metrics include Accuracy, Precision, and Recall. The Ours row shows improvements (in parentheses) over a baseline, and Ours consistently achieves the highest values across all task-language-metric combinations.

supported_claims.claim: Ours achieves the highest Accuracy (34.36%), Precision (37.77%), and Recall (34.38%) for English Sentiment Analysis among all listed methods.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Row 'Ours' and column 'English Acc/Pre/Rec' under 'Sentiment Analysis'

supported_claims.claim: Ours achieves the highest Accuracy (42.11%), Precision (47.59%), and Recall (42.02%) for Chinese Sentiment Analysis among all listed methods.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Row 'Ours' and columns 'Chinese Acc/Pre/Rec' under 'Sentiment Analysis'

supported_claims.claim: Ours outperforms VGG16 in all 12 metric-task-language combinations (Acc, Pre, Rec for each of 4 tasks and 2 languages).
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Comparison of rows 'Ours' and 'VGG16' across all columns

supported_claims.claim: The table includes results for four tasks (Sentiment Analysis, Intention Detection, Offensiveness Detection, Metaphor Recognition) and two languages (English, Chinese).
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Caption: 'Experimental results on the MET-MEME dataset of four tasks.' and row headers indicating tasks and languages

possible_misreadings.claim: The improvement percentages (e.g., +3.89%) show the relative improvement of Ours over the best overall baseline.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: The baseline for the improvement is not explicitly stated; calculations suggest it may be over M3F_add or M3F_cat, but it is inconsistent across metrics and tasks, so the exact baseline is unclear.

possible_misreadings.claim: The table covers all possible tasks on the MET-MEME dataset.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: Only four tasks are listed; the dataset may include additional tasks not shown in this table.

possible_misreadings.claim: All methods are compared fairly without any hyperparameter tuning or dataset splits differences.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: The table does not provide details on experimental settings, such as data splits, number of runs, or statistical significance, so differences may not be reliable.

limitations: Results are limited to the MET-MEME dataset and may not generalize to other datasets.
No statistical significance tests are reported, so performance differences may not be robust.
The baseline for the improvement percentages in the Ours row is not identified, making it unclear what the relative gains are compared to.
Only three metrics (Acc, Pre, Rec) are reported; other relevant metrics like F1-score are omitted.

asset_explanations.caption: Table 2: Ablation results on the MET-MEME English dataset of four tasks. “OM” means object-level semantic mining, “UP” means unimodal prediction, “GL” means global-local interaction, “DG” means dual-semantic guided strategy.
asset_explanations.summary: This table presents ablation results on the MET-MEME English dataset comparing the full model (Ours) against four ablated variants: without object-level semantic mining (w/o OM), without unimodal prediction (w/o UP), without global-local interaction (w/o GL), and without dual-semantic guided strategy (w/o DG). Metrics reported are Accuracy, Precision, and Recall for four tasks: Sentiment Analysis, Intention Detection, Offensiveness Detection, and Metaphor Recognition.

supported_claims.claim: The full model (Ours) achieves the highest Accuracy, Precision, and Recall on all four tasks compared to any ablated variant.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Rows 'Ours' vs 'w/o OM', 'w/o UP', 'w/o GL', 'w/o DG' across all columns (Task, Metric). For each task and metric, the Ours value is greater than all corresponding w/o values. Example: Sentiment Analysis Acc: Ours 34.36 > 32.47 (w/o OM), 32.85 (w/o UP), 31.76 (w/o GL), 33.59 (w/o DG).

supported_claims.claim: Among ablated variants, removing global-local interaction (w/o GL) results in the lowest Accuracy on all four tasks (Sentiment Analysis: 31.76, Intention Detection: 45.82, Offensiveness Detection: 76.89, Metaphor Recognition: 84.98).
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Rows for w/o GL under each task's Acc column: Sentiment Analysis (31.76), Intention Detection (45.82), Offensiveness Detection (76.89), Metaphor Recognition (84.98) are the lowest among all ablated variants.

supported_claims.claim: The dual-semantic guided strategy (w/o DG) causes the smallest drop in Accuracy relative to the full model across all tasks (drops of 0.77, 0.87, 0.37, 1.08 for the four tasks respectively).
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Compute difference between Ours Acc and w/o DG Acc for each task: Sentiment: 34.36-33.59=0.77; Intention: 47.92-47.05=0.87; Offensiveness: 78.11-77.74=0.37; Metaphor: 87.51-86.43=1.08. These are the smallest drops compared to other w/o variants.

possible_misreadings.claim: The ablation study demonstrates that dual-semantic guided strategy is the most important component.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: The table shows that removing global-local interaction (w/o GL) leads to larger performance drops than removing any other component, including dual-semantic guided strategy. Therefore, global-local interaction appears more critical.

possible_misreadings.claim: The model achieves state-of-the-art results on the MET-MEME dataset.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: The table only compares the full model against its own ablated variants, not against any external baselines or prior work. No evidence of state-of-the-art performance is provided.

possible_misreadings.claim: The results are averaged over multiple runs and are statistically significant.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: The table does not report any standard deviations, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. It is unclear if the results are from a single run or aggregated runs.

limitations: Results are only on one dataset (MET-MEME English), limiting generalizability.
No statistical significance or confidence intervals are provided, so the reliability of improvements is unknown.
No comparison to external baselines or prior work is included.
The table does not report standard deviations, so the robustness of the ablation effects is unclear.
